sentences.text: The facts of the leading application are that on 17.12.2022 proceedings came to be initiated under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. by the opposite party no. 2 against the applicant under Section 376 IPC read with Section 4/8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 with an allegation that the victim/complainant was a student of class 10th in the academic year 2018-19 and she came in contact with the applicant herein who was the resident of the same village and they had friendship with each other and the applicant herein allured the opposite party no. 2-victim that he would marry her and while misguiding and creating all sorts of confusion and making false promises, he entered into physical relationship with the victim and when pressure was being mounted post completion of class 12th for getting the marriage solemnized then the applicant refused to get married then the said fact was apprised to the parents of the victim and the parents of the victim approached the applicant's parents for marriage but the same was refused and in the year 2021 the marriage of the victim stood solemnized with one Arvind.

However, post marriage when the victim started a new life then the applicant herein came to the matrimonial house of the opposite party no. 2-victim and showed the videos and pictures depicting intimacy and physical relationship of the applicant with the opposite party no. 2 and also the allegation is that the applicant had threatened the opposite party no. 2 that neither he would marry the opposite party no. 2 nor he would let the opposite party no. 2 either solemnized or lead a married life.
He also threatened that, in case, the victim did not have physical relationship with the applicant then he would get it loaded in the social media so that the entire world would see.

Allegation is that an amount of Rs. 2,50,000/- was being demanded to get the things on a right track on account whereof the victim sustained mental injuries and a complaint was also lodged through registered post on 09.12.2022 before the Superintendent of Police, Sonebhadra and in failing to lodge any FIR, the proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. stood triggered on 17.12.2022.

Post recording of the statements under Section 200 of the victim/complainant and of one Ishwari under Section 202 and Deepak Soni under Section 202, the applicant came to be summoned on 11.07.2024 by the Court of Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO ) Act, Sonebhadra in Complaint Case No. 8 of 2023 under Section 376(2)n IPC read with Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 3. Assailing the summoning order, the leading application came to be filed.
4. As non-bailable warrants came to be issued on 04.01.2025 so the applicant preferred the connected application.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for the simple reason particularly when the entire allegations so sought to be levelled in the complaint are nothing but a bundle of lies just in order to falsely implicate and rope in the complaint.

Submission is that the complaint is vague as there is no date mentioned as to when the alleged offences have been committed and further only the academic year 2018-19 referable to the year when the opposite party no. 2 was studying in class 10th has been mentioned when her modesty was outraged.
Further submission is that there is no date and time of extending false assurance in order to somewhat allure the opposite party no. 2 to get married.

Contention is that even the opposite party no.2-victim was not subjected to any medical examination and, in case,
medical examination ought to have been done and the report was there that the truth would have come on surface.

Further submission is that the entire story so sought to be cooked up by the opposite party no. 2 in the complaint is unbelievable and implorable for the simple reason that Dheeraj Vishwakarma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126560644/
2 alleging false assurance of getting married, thereafter, the opposite party no. 2 solemnized marriage with Arvind and no date, time has been mentioned or even the instance when the said incident took place by which the applicant blackmailed the opposite party no. 2 while forcing her to make physical contact with him otherwise the photographs and the pictures so recorded in the mobile would be made viral.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also contended that no such demand of Rs. 2,50,000/- was made and the entire statements of the victim and of the witnesses under Section 202 are tailor-made just in order to falsely implicate the applicant.
Further, it is also submitted that the victim at the time of alleged incident (though there is no date) was major and, thus, the provisions of the POCSO Act would not apply.
Lastly, it has been submitted that the summoning order has been passed in a routine manner without there being any, prima facie, satisfaction of the commission of offences.

6. Learned AGA, on the other hand, while countering the submission of the learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that at the stage of summoning what would be required would be the allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statement under Section 200 of the victim and of the witnesses under Section 202.

According to him, the statements are in conformity and in consonance with the allegations in the complaint and further there is no material contradiction so as to thoroughly overrule the possibility of attraction of the said penal offences.
7. I have heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

8. In the present case in hand at the instance of the applicant, challenge has been raised to the order passed by Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Sonebhadra on 11.07.2023 summoning the applicant under Section 376(2)n of IPC read with Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act,
2012.

entities.text: Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Sonebhadra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: There are various criteria which needs to be adhered to in order to determine as to whether the summoning order suffers from any illegality or not.
Amongst others, one of the criteria inevitably would be the nature of the allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statements under Sections 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C.

Once there are no material contradictions or variations in the statements vis-a-vis in the complaint and the nature of the complaint alleges criminality as per the penal sections then the case becomes triable.

9. Applying the said principles of law in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it is apparent that proceedings came to be lodged by the opposite party no. 2 on 17.12.2022 against the applicant under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. with an allegation that just in order to have physical intercourse with the opposite party no. 2, the applicant gave false assurance and the opposite party no. 2 being minor was swayed away and physical relationship stood occurred and when request was being made for solemnization of marriage, the applicant herein refused and showed his reluctance pursuant whereto the matter was complained of by the opposite party no. 2 to her parents and when the proposal of marriage was exhibited before the applicant, he refused to get married and thereupon the opposite party no. 2's marriage stood solemnized with one Arvind, however, the opposite party no. 2 alleges to have been blackmailed for having physical relationship otherwise the photos and videos would have been made viral.
The prosecution theory stands supported from the bare look of the statement of the victim under Section 200 and of the witnesses under Section 202 Cr.P.C.
The next question which would arise that would be what would be the impact and the effect of non-subjection of medication examination of the opposite party no. 2.

As a matter of fact, the Dheeraj Vishwakarma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126560644/
3 issue as to whether the opposite party no. 2 was medically examined or not and what would be the impact would be a question which would necessitate consideration at the stage when the trial commences when a decision is to be taken as to whether the accused is to be convicted or acquitted.

sentences.text: With respect to allegation that there are no specific date on which the physical relationship took place and the modesty of the opposite party no. 2 was outraged is a question which would need discussion and its importance is to be weighed at the stage when the trial commences.
At the stage of summoning what is required is the, prima facie, satisfaction of the Court that there has been happened to be a case which is triable.
The question as to whether there is any merit in the allegations so sought to be levelled by the prosecution/victim is a question which needs adjudication at the stage when trial commences.
There is another facet of the matter which also needs consideration at this stage i.e. Section 29 of the POCSO Act.

Section 29 deals with presumption as to certain offences according to which where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under Sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of the Act, the special court is to presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence as the case may be unless the contrary is proved.
The word employed by the legislature contrary is proved "mark significance" as the same pre-supposes a trial.

As regards the submission of the learned counsel for the applicant that the opposite party no. 2 was major when the alleged offences have been committed (though disputed) the Court is not required to delve into the said issues at this stage as the question with regard to the fact as to whether the opposite party no. 2 was minor or major would depend upon leading of evidence which would be subject matter of trial.

10. The Hon?ble Apex Court in M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, AIR 2021 SC 1918 had the occasion to consider the ambit and the extent of intervention under Article 482 Cr.P.C. wherein it was observed as under:-
?23.

sentences.text: Therefore, when the investigation by the police is in progress, the court should not go into the merits of the allegations in the FIR.
Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.
It would be premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

After investigation, if the investigating officer finds that there is no substance in the application made by the complainant, the investigating officer may file an appropriate report/summary before the learned Magistrate which may be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with the known procedure;
xiii) The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be more cautious.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: xiv) However, at the same time, the court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self-restraint imposed by law, more particularly the parameters laid down by this Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur (supra) and Bhajan Lal (supra), has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/complaint;

xv) When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged accused and the court when it exercises the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether the allegations in the FIR disclose commission of a cognizable offence or not.

The court is not required to consider on merits whether or not the merits of the allegations make out a cognizable offence and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR;
xvi) The aforesaid parameters would be applicable and/or the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered by the High Court while passing an interim order in a quashing petition in exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

However,
an interim order of stay of investigation during the pendency of the quashing petition can be passed with circumspection.
Such an interim order should not require to be passed routinely, casually and/or mechanically.

Normally, when the investigation is in progress and the facts are hazy and the entire evidence/material is not before the High Court, the High Court should restrain itself from passing the interim order of not to arrest or ?no coercive steps to be adopted? and the accused should be relegated to apply for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. before the competent court.

The High Court shall not and as such is not justified in passing the order of not to arrest and/or ?no coercive steps? either during the investigation or till the investigation is completed and/or till the final report/chargesheet is filed under Section 173 Cr.P.C., while dismissing/disposing of the quashing petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

xvii) Even in a case where the High Court is prima facie of the opinion that an exceptional case is made out for grant of interim stay of further investigation, after considering the broad parameters while exercising the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India referred to hereinabove, the High Court has to give brief reasons why such an interim order is warranted and/or is required to be passed so that it can demonstrate the application of mind by the Court and the higher forum can consider what was weighed with the High Court while passing such an interim order.

xviii) Whenever an interim order is passed by the High Court of ?no coercive steps to be adopted?
within the aforesaid parameters, the High Court must clarify what does it mean by ?no coercive steps to be adopted? as the term ?no coercive steps to be adopted? can be said to be too vague and/or broad which can be misunderstood and/or misapplied.?
11. Analysing the case from four corners of law, this Court does not find the present case to be a fit case for interference in exercise of inherent jurisdiction.
12.
Accordingly, the leading application is rejected 13.
Since the leading application stands rejected, thus, the connected application wherein non-bailable warrants have been questioned also stands rejected.
